claims.text: Repeated arc melting refines and homogenizes the microstructure of WTaTiVZr.
The refined and homogenized microstructure produced by repeated arc melting primarily controls high-temperature plastic strain and toughness in WTaTiVZr.
Repeated arc melting causes dynamic recrystallization in WTaTiVZr.
Repeated arc melting produces fine, equiaxed grains in WTaTiVZr.
Repeated arc melting produces a uniform dispersion of secondary phases in WTaTiVZr.
Fine grains increase grain-boundary area in WTaTiVZr.
Increased grain-boundary area enhances high-temperature dislocation activity.
Dispersed secondary phases can act as effective dislocation sources.
Fine grains and dispersed secondary phases retard crack propagation.
Enhanced dislocation activity and retarded crack propagation improve high-temperature plastic strain capacity and toughness.
Repeatedly arc-melted WTaTiVZr will have greater high-temperature strain to failure than similarly processed pure tungsten.
Repeatedly arc-melted WTaTiVZr will have higher high-temperature fracture toughness than similarly processed pure tungsten.
The predicted mechanical improvements will correlate with observable microstructural refinement.
Pure tungsten remains coarser and less refined than WTaTiVZr when processed under similar conditions.
The proposed mechanism applies between approximately 1000°C and 1800°C under mechanical loading relevant to fusion plasma-facing applications.
The proposed relationship may not hold for materials or processing routes that do not produce comparable microstructural refinement.
